Quickstart

Every integration wraps the same run: guard, think, plan, act, write. A call returns the written answer plus the citation list that backs each claim. Nothing is returned that is not tied to a record.

curl https://api.ncbi-agentic-search.org/v1/query \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NCBI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"question": "What is the clinical significance of rs334?"}'

What comes back

{
  "run_id": "run_8f2c41",
  "status": "answered",
  "answer": "rs334 is a missense variant in HBB ...",
  "claims": [{"text": "...", "layer": 2, "citations": ["clinvar:VCV000015333"]}],
  "citations": [{"id": "clinvar:VCV000015333", "layer": 2, "tool": "ncbi_efetch"}],
  "tools_run": 7, "layers": [1, 2, 3], "elapsed_ms": 18400
}

A refused question returns status: "refused" with a reason and an empty citation list. It is a 200, not an error.

Access

The web interface is open: ask questions without an account, up to the free allowance. The programmatic surfaces, REST and SSE, MCP, the command line and the KGX export, need a signed-in account.

How a program presents that account is not settled yet. It will reuse the NCBI API key that is already part of this system rather than introducing a second, separate credential of its own.

export NCBI_API_KEY=your-ncbi-api-key

Store it in an environment variable, never in a repository.

REST and SSE

Post a question, then either wait for the completed run or subscribe to the event stream and render the run as it happens, exactly as the web interface does.

EndpointPurpose
POST /v1/queryStart a run. Returns run_id immediately, or the full answer with wait=true.
GET /v1/query/{run_id}Fetch a completed run.
GET /v1/query/{run_id}/eventsSSE stream of the run, resumable with Last-Event-ID.
GET /v1/query/{run_id}/citationsCitation list with layer, tool and record URL.
POST /v1/query/{run_id}/follow_upContinue a thread. Runs a full search; prior context is used only where relevant.

Event stream

event: guard    data: {"verdict":"in_scope"}
event: plan     data: {"calls":7,"layers":[1,2,3]}
event: tool     data: {"name":"ncbi_dbsnp","status":"ok","ms":840}
event: claim    data: {"text":"...","layer":2,"citations":["clinvar:VCV000015333"]}
event: done     data: {"status":"answered","elapsed_ms":18400}

MCP server

The server advertises one tool. A client model asks a biomedical question and receives a finished, cited answer; the seven internal tools and the planner are never exposed, so a client cannot compose a partial run.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ncbi-search": {
      "url": "https://api.ncbi-agentic-search.org/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${NCBI_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}

Tool

FieldDetail
nameask_biomedical_question
questionRequired string. Out-of-scope questions return a refusal, not an error.
max_layersOptional 1–3. Caps how deep the run goes.
returnsanswer, claims, citations, tools_run, elapsed_ms

KGX export

The graph layer as BioLink-compliant KGX, for loading into your own store. Node and edge files are gzipped TSV; the snapshot date matches the one cited in answers.

GET /v1/export/kgx?format=tsv&since=2026-07-14
GET /v1/export/kgx/run/{run_id}   # just the subgraph one run touched
FileContents
nodes.tsv.gz115M nodes: id, category, name, xrefs, source database.
edges.tsv.gz693M edges: subject, predicate, object, evidence, provenance.
manifest.jsonSnapshot date, source versions, licence per source.

Public domain for the NCBI-derived layers. Literature and trial enrichment carries publisher terms; those rows are marked in the manifest.

Command line

The same run, piped. Output is human-readable by default and JSON with --json, so answers can be chained into other tools.

pip install ncbi-agentic-search
export NCBI_API_KEY=your-ncbi-api-key

ncbi-search ask "diseases linked to BRCA1"
ncbi-search ask "clinical significance of rs334" --json | jq '.citations'
ncbi-search watch run_8f2c41        # attach to a running query
ncbi-search export kgx --since 2026-07-14
FlagEffect
--jsonMachine-readable run object.
--layers 1,2Restrict which data layers may be used.
--cite-onlyPrint the citation list and nothing else.

Limits and errors

TierLimit
Guest5 questions per browser session, web interface only.
Account60 questions per hour, 5 concurrent runs.
InstitutionalNegotiated. Contact the team for a raised ceiling.

Rate state is returned on every response in X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset.

StatusMeaning
401Missing or revoked key.
429Rate limit reached. Retry after the reset header.
504An upstream NCBI service did not answer. The run is kept and can be resumed.

A question the guard rejects is not an error. It returns 200 with status: "refused" and the reason, so clients can show it as an answer rather than a failure.

How an answer is built

Every question crosses up to three data layers. The colour on a citation tells you which layer it came from and therefore how fresh it is and how it was established.

Knowledge graph

L1

115M nodes and 693M edges merged from 5 NCBI databases. Broad and fast, but a periodic snapshot rather than live.

Live NCBI APIs

L2

E-utilities, Datasets and dbSNP, called at the moment you ask. Narrower and slower, and always current.

Enrichment

L3

PubTator3, LitVar2 and ClinicalTrials.gov. Literature and trial evidence layered on a fact the first two layers established.

The run loop

The same five stages run for every question, and the run screen shows them as they happen. Nothing is hidden behind a spinner: the reasoning panel logs each stage with a timestamp, and that log stays attached to the answer under Show work.

1Guard

Decides whether the question can be grounded in NCBI records at all. Requests for diagnosis, treatment advice, or anything outside biomedicine are refused here, before a single tool runs and without spending a search.

2Think

Resolves the entities in the question to identifiers — a gene symbol to an NCBI Gene id, an rs number to a RefSNP — and classifies what kind of answer the question needs.

3Plan

Chooses which tools to call and in what order, working from the curated layers outward. A question answerable from the graph alone does not spend live calls.

4Act

Runs the calls, each one reported with what it returned. A tool that fails or returns nothing is shown as such rather than quietly dropped.

5Write

Maps every claim to at least one retrieved record. A claim with no record behind it is dropped rather than written, which is why some runs end with no answer.

The tool set

A run uses only what the question needs. The rs334 example calls most of these; a trials question calls one.

ToolLayerReturns
cypher_queryL1Curated edges between genes, variants and conditions, with the evidence code that established each one.
ncbi_dbsnpL2Variant normalisation (SPDI, HGVS and genomic position, so every later call resolves the same allele) plus allele frequency by population cohort.
ncbi_efetchL2Full records from ClinVar, Gene, MedGen, PubMed and related databases, including review status, submission counts, condition definitions and inheritance patterns.
litvar2_lookupL3Publications that mention a specific variant, matched on identifier rather than on free text.
pubtator_annotateL3Entity co-mentions in the literature, used where no curated record covers the link.
clinicaltrials_searchL3Registered studies filtered by condition, intervention and recruitment status.

Cite or refuse

Every claim is tied to a specific record. When nothing supports an answer, the system says so and stops rather than answering from memory. The track beside each answer shows one segment per claim, coloured by its layer, so an uncited claim is visible before you read a word.

Sources are listed in full under every answer: the tool that fetched them, the evidence type, the confidence, and a link to the record itself. If a citation does not support the claim it is attached to, flag it from the source list and the pair goes to the review queue.

What it will not do

  • Give diagnosis, prognosis, or treatment recommendations for a person.
  • Answer from the model's own memory when retrieval comes back empty.
  • Present a literature co-mention as though it were a curated classification.
  • Resolve a disagreement between layers silently — conflicts are shown, not averaged.

Coverage varies by organism and by database. Treat every answer as a starting point for verification, not an endpoint.

Before you start

This tool answers research questions. It does not give medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment recommendations.

Answers are assembled from NCBI records and cited back to them. Always speak to a qualified health professional about a medical condition.
